runtime.execution: Async FastMCP HTTP service; SQLite/SQLAlchemy sessions, worker-thread Git filesystem operations and awaited commit queue. It does not run the participating agents.
runtime.service_boundary: Owns mail identities/index/archive and advisory reservations. Client coding agents and their programs/provider requests remain separately owned.

summary: Addressed persistent mail with authenticated identities, per-recipient read/ack, cross-project contacts and advisory file reservations.

inspection.scope: registration/authentication, send/store/notification, inbox/ack/search, advisory reservation, macro, settings and selected test assertions
inspection.limits: No client agent turn/provider loop or commercial Companion implementation was inspected; partial filesystem/Git crash recovery is not proven.

actions.name: register_agent / macro_start_session
actions.surface: external model MCP tool or operator/client API
actions.input: Project identity, external program/model, optional name/token/task and reservation/inbox options.
actions.output: Durable identity/profile plus registration token; macro returns reservations and mail.
actions.lifecycle: Register or update persistent identity; reconnect authentication binds current MCP session; does not start model work.
actions.authority: Bearer/JWT endpoint access plus token/session binding for an existing identity.

actions.name: send_message
actions.input: Project/sender token, to/cc/bcc or broadcast, subject/body, thread/topic, attachments, importance/ack.
actions.output: Delivery list/count, native message IDs or contact/archive/conflict errors.
actions.lifecycle: DB then awaited archive; blocked contact never queues body; signals are hints; recipient busy status is not consulted.
actions.authority: Authenticated sender, contact policy and visible recipient scope; external clients govern when mail enters their context.

actions.name: fetch_inbox / acknowledge_message
actions.input: Recipient/token, limit/time/topic/urgent/unread filters; explicit message ID for ack.
actions.output: Recent metadata/optional bodies and per-recipient read/ack timestamps.
actions.lifecycle: Polling leaves unread state intact; explicit ack is idempotent receipt, not execution completion.
actions.authority: Authenticated recipient and visible addressed message.

actions.name: search_messages
actions.input: Authenticated project identity, FTS5 query and capped result limit.
actions.output: Ranked visible message metadata; parameterized LIKE fallback or empty invalid-query result.
actions.lifecycle: Queries persistent index without replaying an agent; source originals separately accessible in archive.
actions.authority: Sender-or-recipient visibility predicate on both query branches.

actions.name: file_reservation_paths
actions.input: Identity token, project-relative paths/globs, exclusive flag, TTL/reason.
actions.output: Granted reservation IDs/expiry/reused marker plus overlapping holders and advisory warning.
actions.lifecycle: May grant while conflicting; renew/release are separately named lifecycle tools; new rows compensated on archive error.
actions.authority: Intent signals; code write access is not fenced, optional precommit guard acts at commit.

actions.name: summarize_thread
actions.input: Thread IDs, per-thread limit, optional examples/LLM mode/model.
actions.output: Heuristic points/actions/mentions plus optional model refinement.
actions.lifecycle: On-demand derived digest; preserves stored mail rather than compacting a client conversation.
actions.authority: Authenticated visible mail and server-configured LLM availability.

actions.name: clear_settings_cache
actions.output: Cache cleared; next get_settings builds new Settings.
actions.lifecycle: Explicit next-access refresh; captured server objects need their own recreation.
actions.authority: Service-side code, not an exposed arbitrary model turn rewrite.

evidence.claim: register_agent accepts project/program/model/name/task/attachment metadata and registration token; profiles describe external agents rather than creating a provider loop.
Identity operations require an authenticated session or constant-time registration-token match; tokenless legacy cleanup and configured window rebind are special cases.
send_message accepts addressed/broadcast Markdown, attachments, thread/topic/ack and sender token; blocked automatic contact does not queue message body and requires a new send.
Processed message commits in DB before Git bundle; archive exception triggers best-effort DB compensation. Notification after archive lock is best effort and is not model interruption.
Canonical/outbox and recipient inbox copies carry JSON frontmatter; recipient BCC is redacted and body is stripped, attachments processed; writing files/digest precedes awaited Git commit.
Commit queue enqueue waits for request future; absent/stopped/full processor falls back to direct commit, so ordinary completion does not just enqueue archive publication.
Debounced per-agent signal file overwrites one notification projection; errors return false and do not fail mail delivery.
fetch_inbox authenticates recipient, filters/caps recent mail and does not mark read/ack; it clears best-effort notification signal after polling.
acknowledge_message checks visibility and stores recipient read and ack timestamps separately; it represents receipt, not task execution.
Authenticated scoped FTS search limits sender/recipient visibility and returns ranked subject/body matches; unsupported/syntax queries are handled separately.
FTS failure falls back to parameterized AND-term LIKE query over visible messages, with limit and creation-time ordering; returned records contain metadata.
Overlapping exclusive reservation conflicts are reported while reservations are still granted; DB commit then archive with compensation for new rows only; code-path advisory warning is explicit.

Reservation API accepts paths/globs, TTL, exclusive intent and identity token; server archive enforcement and code precommit guard are distinct. Sub-minute TTL actually warns rather than enforcing the docstring minimum.
macro_start_session authenticates existing identity, ensures project/registers new identity, invokes reservation tool and fetches inbox; result includes token, agent, reservations and mail.
Thread digest combines heuristic points/actions and optional enabled LLM refinement; only compact derived thread summaries reach refinement; failure falls back without replacing stored messages.
Explicit settings accessor cache reset reloads configuration next access; no automatic full server/transport/client reconfiguration is demonstrated.
HTTP middleware checks static bearer in constant time, optional local bypass or inner JWT delegation; endpoint auth is distinct from agent identity.

tests.oracle: Read test1209–1252: monkeypatched bundle raises, asserts actual Message and MessageRecipient row counts are both zero. Good compensation oracle; fails before partial file writes and does not model crash/fsync or compensation failure.
Read test110–185 and825–872: exact prior read/ack timestamps are retained; native ID/subject/self-inbox assertions. They validate logical receipt, not model execution or notification reliability.

Read1–170: block_all raises specific error, overlapping reservations allow intended contact and addressed cross-project payload appears. Same MCP client can bind several identities; not evidence every remote client has that identity.

strengths: Separates durable message from transient signal and explicit recipient receipt.
Source filters both primary and fallback searches by actual visibility.
Awaited Git queue and DB compensation are concrete rather than only an enqueue acknowledgement.
Reservation response discloses conflict and code-path advisory mode.
limits: Mail receipt is not completion or interruption of recipient work.
Archive body/attachments are transformed; no client provider original audit.
DB/Git/filesystem publication is non-atomic and compensation is best effort.
Conflicting exclusive code reservations still grant; external guard cannot fence all writes.
Settings reset is not executable reload/refit; commercial Companion behavior remains unavailable.
arconaut_questions: Can a consumer mailbox distinguish stored, offered, incorporated, and acted-on messages without confusing provider quiescence with mail delivery?
How should audit retain the original submitted body/attachments alongside canonical readable projections?
Should model/operator coordination avoid exclusive-intent labels unless the filesystem effects are actually fenced?
